text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
QADISSIYA
- President Saddam Hussein chairs cabinet meeting and urges ministers to formulate plan for new cadres to take over from old ones.
- Saddam sends message to Sudanese president.
- United States blocked spare parts from reaching Iraq.
- Ship loaded with wheat arrives at Umm Qasr in southern Iraq.
- Condemnation of Turkish invasion of northern Iraq continues.
- Italy keen to develop ties with Iraq.
- Vice-Chairman of Revolutionary Command Council Ibrahim holds meeting with harvest committees.
- Iraq and Belgium review parliamentary ties.
- Deputy Prime Minister Aziz receives Belgian parliamentary delegation.
- Trade delegation leaves for Jordan.
(The above were also carried by JUMHOURIYA and AL-IRAQ)
- Article shows link between next census and economic development in Iraq in 21st Century.
- Article attempts to prove that Iraq's socialist system is different from that pursued by communists.
JUMHOURIYA
- Iraqi-Turkish gas pipeline to be implemented soon.
- Police capture gang of thieves accused of 108 burglaries.
AL-IRAQ
- Local industries help offset impact of U.N. trade sanctions.
- No legal basis for air embargo on Iraq.
